To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Sickle cell disease is associated with myocardial ischemic injury; (2) cardiac magnetic resonance can detect microvascular obstruction in sickle cell disease; (3) myocardial infarction in sickle cell patients can be under-diagnosed; (4) cardiac magnetic resonance may be a useful tool in the diagnosis of myocardial infarctions in patients with sickle cell disease.

CMR may be useful in diagnosing and characterizing myocardial infarction in sickle cell disease patients with chest pain, and that CMR may help guide clinical management decisions for patients with SCD who present with chest pain.
myocardial infarction is under-diagnosed in SCD patients, and that CMR can be used to diagnose MI in SCD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a potentially under-recognized problem in Sickle Cell disease: Myocardial Infarctions.
the use of translational imaging in the diagnosis of an under-recognized problem in SCD.
the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SCD is a multisystem disease, with the potential for microvascular disease to cause myocardial ischemia.
the incidence of MI and myocardial infarction in SCD remains unknown and is likely underestimated.
SCD patients presenting with acute chest pain should undergo CMR to assess for MI, and that CMR is uniquely suited to detect myocardial microvascular disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SCD patients with chest pain and/or ECG findings suggestive of MI should be evaluated with CMR.
the use of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMRs) can be a useful tool in diagnosing and treating myocardial infarction in sickle cell patients.
SCD is a disease with high risk of sudden death, and CMR can be used to diagnose MI, a potential contributor to that risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with chest pain.
CMR is an invaluable imaging tool for the evaluation of patients with chest pain and SCD.
CMR is uniquely suited to detect microvascular disease in SCD and may help define the prevalence and natural history of ischemic heart disease.
